title: Dark circles under the eyes
question_forms: How do I treat dark circles and eye bags on dark skin?
Why do I have dark circles under my eyes?
Do eye creams work for dark circles?
tradition_says: Dark circles are blamed on tiredness and treated with sleep, cold spoons, cucumber and eye creams.

layer1.plain_answer: Dark circles under the eyes can come from pigment, thin skin showing blood vessels, or lost volume, and the cause decides the treatment. A systematic review found many treatments help some people, from creams and peels to fillers, but the studies are weak and not specific to Black skin. Daily sunscreen is a sensible start.

do.text: Ask a dermatologist to work out which kind you have: pigment, structure, blood vessels or a mix.
Apply sunscreen daily, SPF 30 or higher, broad-spectrum.

source.name: American Academy of Dermatology, "Skin care tips dermatologists use"

do.text: For pigment-type circles, creams and peels are the treatments the review found useful.

avoid.text: Expecting one cream to fix every kind: fillers or fat grafting suit volume loss, surgery suits loose skin, creams suit pigment.
Taking any claim on trust: the review calls the evidence scarce and weak and says to read recommendations selectively.

see_someone_when: Swelling, pain or vision changes around the eyes (doctor urgently).
Circles that appeared suddenly, are one-sided, or follow a new medicine (doctor).
You are considering fillers, lasers or surgery (dermatologist or an accredited specialist).

tested.population: Participants in 39 studies of periorbital hyperpigmentation; groups not stated in the abstract
tested.finding: Fillers and fat grafting work best for dark circles from volume loss; blepharoplasty for loose skin; creams and peels for pigment; lasers mildly to moderately for vascular and pigment types. The authors note the scarcity of high-quality evidence and ask for more randomised trials.

source.authors: Michelle L, Pouldar Foulad D, Ekelem C et al

tier_driver: That the cause decides the treatment, from one systematic review that its authors call low in quality, with no data specific to Black skin.
tier_note: Review of poor-quality studies in unspecified populations. Common home remedies (cold compresses, tea bags, cucumber, sleep) are untested in what I opened.
harm_note: No harm signal in the abstract; invasive treatments carry their own risks that were not reviewed here.
evidence_summary: The review of 39 studies lists pigmentary, structural, vascular and mixed causes. It says fillers and fat grafting help volume-loss circles, surgery helps loose skin, topical creams and peels help pigment-type, and lasers help mildly to moderately, but quality is low and it does not report skin type.
measured_variables: Skin pigmentation (not reported in the review)
gaps: Untested or not found: home remedies (sleep, cold compresses, tea bags); trials in Black skin; which creams (vitamin C, retinol, kojic acid) work. UK-specific guidance on dark circles was not found in my search.

sources.name: American Academy of Dermatology, "Skin care tips dermatologists use"
